name: Public Image Ltd
hook: Took dub's empty space and bass pressure into rock and removed almost everything else.
blurb: After the Sex Pistols ended, John Lydon started a band with a bass player, Jah Wobble, who had learned from Jamaican sound systems. On 'Metal Box' the bass is enormous and low and sits where the vocal would normally be, the guitar is scraping metal, and there is far more silence than a rock record usually allows. It is punk energy arranged like a dub record. PiL show the move from dub to post-punk more completely than the Clash, because they borrowed how dub is built rather than how it sounds on the surface. The record was first sold in a metal film canister.

signatureTracks.title: Death Disco
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Built around Jah Wobble's bassline and released while Lydon's mother was dying, proof the dub-derived sound could carry the band's most personal material.

signatureTracks.title: Careering
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Bass as lead instrument, synthesizer as noise, and space where the arrangement should be.
